description: PlutusData (datum/redeemer) CBOR canonicalization + decode-strictness differential (cardano 11.1.2 vs amaru 0925). Non-canonical/malformed PlutusData spliced into a redeemer or supplied datum (body untouched). Result: canonical controls accept on both; every non-canonical variant rejects on both -- the >64-byte chunk limit at DECODE (both), the rest via the script-integrity hash (both). No decode/datum-hash/is_valid divergence. Boundary: pure decoder-acceptance (non-canonical WITH a matching integrity hash) needs the integrity-hash recomputation lane; not isolated here.

cases.note: spend datum-hash UTxO with canonical supplied datum (control) -> both accept
redeemer unit as tag121+INDEFINITE array -> both reject (integrity hash); decode-lenient on both
redeemer tag121 via non-minimal 2-byte arg -> both reject (integrity hash)
redeemer int 0 as non-minimal uint64 -> both reject (integrity hash)
redeemer bytestring via indefinite chunks -> both reject (integrity hash)
redeemer map with DUPLICATE key -> both DECODE-accept then reject (integrity hash); neither strict-rejects dup keys at decode
redeemer 65-byte bytestring in ONE chunk (>64) -> both DECODE-REJECT (64-byte PlutusData chunk limit enforced identically)
datum-hash spend with NON-canonical supplied datum -> both reject (integrity hash catches it)
